learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparing numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected 100 km/h for equivalent wall speed, then locked it in.
observations.exploration: Into a car at 50 produced 145 kJ and car A 50 to 0 at fixed meeting point. Into a wall at 50 retained 145 kJ; wall at 100 produced 579 kJ. Retained comparison labels car 50:145, wall 50:145, wall 100:579; reveal unlocked.
observations.reveal: Corrected to 50 km/h. Explains fixed meeting point, each car stopping in its own crumple zone, total two-car energy shared, speed-squared crush energy.
observations.visual: Inline screenshots inspected for initial, car50, wall50, wall100. Colored energy bar stayed same for car50 and wall50 then lengthened about fourfold at wall100; comparison markers retained. Cars stop at centre; rigid wall replaces second car.
observations.isolation: Preview no-history banner present; 5/5 trust counter ignored.
references: CUA tab 543884107 snapshots and four inline screenshots; no screenshot file saved.

prediction.reason: Precise identical-car setup surfaces closing-speed misconception.

interaction.reason: Controlled target contrast and doubled-speed comparison expose equality and quadratic difference with retained markers.
interaction.evidence: Car50 and wall50 both145 kJ; wall100579 kJ screenshots.

payoff.reason: Explicitly links observed energy bars and meeting point to each crumple zone.
payoff.evidence: Reveal cites all three measurements and equal-car symmetry.

clarity.reason: Named target/speed controls and retained labels make comparison legible.

transfer.reason: Reusable squared-speed principle offered, but no new application or conditions beyond identical cars and rigid wall setup.
transfer.evidence: Speed-squared reveal sentence and initial assumptions.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard, focus, contrast audit, phone, zoom/reflow and motion unknown.

surprise.reason: 100 prediction contradicted by equal car50/wall50 bars.

visualExplanation.reason: Fixed meeting point and retained bar comparisons carry mechanism over three states.

playfulness.reason: Target and speed buttons permit reversible crash comparisons.

practicalValue.reason: Speed-risk comparison concrete, without a separate decision task.

depth.reason: Equal-car symmetry and quadratic speed dependence are distinct linked relations.

complexity.reason: Tracks per-car energy versus total energy and squared-speed relation with visual support.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Two linked energy comparisons and symmetry.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: moderate: crush energy and crumple zones
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: moderate: kJ, km/h and factor-of-four comparison

whyCool: Changing only the target from identical car to wall leaves the 145 kJ bar unchanged, while doubling speed stretches it to 579 kJ.
caveat: No unequal-car or non-rigid-wall case tested; equivalence depends on the stated identical-car setup.
